text:
Sam (Support): hey team, Envoy Labs just finished the self-serve onboarding flow but they report they don't see an API key in the console. customer says they get 403s from their app. I can repro from the console for their project (envoy-prod) — Keys tab shows 0 keys, but provisioning logs look like a key was created. org_id=org_98765, project_slug=envoy-prod, customer_email=ops@envoylabs.com :wave:

InfraBot: provisioning-service: created api_key ak_live_7c9b for org_id=org_98765 target_project=legacy-org-4321 status=SUCCESS request_id=prov-43ef9

Mica (Onboarding): thanks Sam. can you paste the customer account id + the console project id (the numeric project id we use internally)? also any trace ids from their 403s.

Sam (Support): account: acct_67890, project_id: 43321, 403 trace from the app: trace=6f2a1b. repro steps i used: 1) sign in as support impersonate acct_67890 2) go to Projects > envoy-prod 3) Keys tab -> empty.

Jordan (SRE): quick look — provisioning record shows the key created but attached to `legacy-org-4321` (different project id). probable cause: provisioning job picks the first matching project for that org slug when org canonical mapping is ambiguous. we have a duplicate slug mapping for that customer because they previously had a sandbox org created (org_11223) with the same slug. internal query that matched: ```SELECT id FROM projects WHERE slug='envoy-prod' AND org_id IN (SELECT id FROM orgs WHERE name ilike '%envoy%') ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1;``` That ORDER BY created_at returns the old sandbox project. manual fix is to rebind the key to the correct project id: ```adminctl keys rebind --key ak_live_7c9b --to-project 43321 --actor mica_onboard```

Mica (Onboarding): running the rebind now...

Mica (Onboarding): rebind completed — output: `OK: key ak_live_7c9b now bound to project 43321` :thumbsup: I also added a quick note to the customer's onboarding ticket explaining the fix.

Sam (Support): replied to customer with: "Hi — we found the key, it was provisioned into an older sandbox project. We've moved it to your envoy-prod project (project id 43321). You should see it in Console > envoy-prod > Keys. Please restart your service and confirm the 403s are cleared. Apologies for the hiccup. — Sam"

Katie (Customer Success): thanks — please confirm with the customer when they validate. also this looks like a platform bug (race/ambiguous-org mapping) — can we get a JIRA? add severity P3 for now.

Jordan (SRE): created JIRA INFR-4128: "Provisioning binds keys to incorrect project when org slug is ambiguous (sandbox/legacy duplicate)" and added repro steps + logs. link: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-4128. I'll own the remediation: we'll change the provisioning query to require explicit org_id when provided, and add a sanity check that the target project org_id === requested org_id.

Mica (Onboarding): also updated the onboarding runbook (internal doc) with a troubleshooting checklist: how to check provisioning record, `adminctl keys rebind` snippet, and a note to confirm `org_id` vs `org_slug`.

Sam (Support): customer replied: "thanks Sam — keys visible now and service is back online. appreciate the quick help." closing loop.

Jordan (SRE): leaving a note — follow-up: we should add an alert when provisioning job returns a target_project that doesn't match the requested project_id for >1% of runs in a day. tagging @mica_onboard to ensure we include the check in the oncall runbook.

Katie (Customer Success): great. filing a short postmortem template into the ticket and will follow up with the account team to ensure the customer gets a summary. :white_check_mark:
